records.Japanese:

船もずいぶん停泊して賑わっているな…
ん、何だ？

records.english: Alexandria... Quite a few ships in port. Hm? What's that?

records.Japanese:
…ああ、これも違う
愛しの『エリュシオン号』！
どこだ！　どこにいるんだあ！

records.english: No... Not this one, either. My beloved Elysion! Where are you!?

records.Japanese: 何か探しているんですかね？

records.english: Is he looking for something?

records.Japanese:
そのようだな
おい、何か探しているのか？

records.Japanese:
船を探しているのであります
我が『エリュシオン号』を！

records.english: My ship, sir! My Elysion!

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.context: Hodram invites Cesare to join the crew and keep looking for his lost ship. Cesare offers a practical lesson on choosing ships. Hodram can hear the whole lesson or excuse him to make departure preparations.
records.source_meaning: Hodram reacts questioningly.
records.localization_note: Hodram's silent question lets Cesare explain the loss.

records.Japanese:
かつて私と『エリュシオン号』は
７つの海を渡っておりました
records.speaker: Cesare Tony
records.context: Hodram invites Cesare to join the crew and keep looking for his lost ship. Cesare offers a practical lesson on choosing ships. Hodram can hear the whole lesson or excuse him to make departure preparations.
records.source_meaning: The man and that ship once sailed the seven seas.
records.localization_note: Preserve Cesare's affectionate pairing of himself with his ship and keep the familiar expression together.
records.previous_English: The Elysion and I once sailed the seven seas.
records.english: The Elysion and I once sailed the seven seas.

records.Japanese:
ところが、海賊に襲われてしまい
私は助かりましたが
『エリュシオン号』は奪われてしまい…
records.speaker: Cesare Tony
records.context: Hodram invites Cesare to join the crew and keep looking for his lost ship. Cesare offers a practical lesson on choosing ships. Hodram can hear the whole lesson or excuse him to make departure preparations.

records.english: But pirates attacked us. I survived, but they took the Elysion...

records.Japanese: それで、その船を探している、と？

records.context: Hodram invites Cesare to join the crew and keep looking for his lost ship. Cesare offers a practical lesson on choosing ships. Hodram can hear the whole lesson or excuse him to make departure preparations.
records.source_meaning: Charles confirms that this is why he is searching.
records.localization_note: Charles checks that the lost ship is the goal of the search.
records.previous_English: So you're searching for it?
records.english: So you're searching for it?

records.Japanese:
ええ、様々な港を探しているのですが…
いまだ…
records.speaker: Cesare Tony
records.context: Hodram invites Cesare to join the crew and keep looking for his lost ship. Cesare offers a practical lesson on choosing ships. Hodram can hear the whole lesson or excuse him to make departure preparations.
records.source_meaning: He has searched various ports without finding it yet.
records.localization_note: The repeated unsuccessful search makes Cesare's frustration plain.
records.previous_English: Yes. I've searched port after port, but... Nothing yet.
records.english: Yes. I've searched port after port, but... Nothing yet.

records.Japanese:
…『７つの海を渡っていた』と言うが
世界中を航海したということか？

records.context: Hodram invites Cesare to join the crew and keep looking for his lost ship. Cesare offers a practical lesson on choosing ships. Hodram can hear the whole lesson or excuse him to make departure preparations.
records.source_meaning: Hodram asks whether sailing the seven seas means he has traveled around the world.

records.english: Seven seas? You sailed the whole world?

records.Japanese:
ええ、アジアに新大陸…

records.speaker: Cesare Tony
records.context: Hodram invites Cesare to join the crew and keep looking for his lost ship. Cesare offers a practical lesson on choosing ships. Hodram can hear the whole lesson or excuse him to make departure preparations.
records.source_meaning: He confirms travels through Asia, the New World and many countries.

records.english: Yes. Asia, the New World, many lands.

records.Japanese: 船での役職は？
records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.context: Hodram invites Cesare to join the crew and keep looking for his lost ship. Cesare offers a practical lesson on choosing ships. Hodram can hear the whole lesson or excuse him to make departure preparations.
records.source_meaning: Hodram asks his shipboard position.
records.localization_note: Hodram's terse question asks about Cesare's shipboard role.
records.previous_English: Your post?
records.english: Your post?

records.Japanese: もちろん、艦長であります！
records.speaker: Cesare Tony
records.context: Hodram invites Cesare to join the crew and keep looking for his lost ship. Cesare offers a practical lesson on choosing ships. Hodram can hear the whole lesson or excuse him to make departure preparations.
records.source_meaning: He proudly states that he was the captain.
records.localization_note: Cesare gives his original rank confidently, answering Hodram directly.

records.english: Captain, of course!

records.Japanese: 各地の知識と艦長経験…か
records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.context: Hodram invites Cesare to join the crew and keep looking for his lost ship. Cesare offers a practical lesson on choosing ships. Hodram can hear the whole lesson or excuse him to make departure preparations.
records.source_meaning: Hodram weighs the local knowledge and captain's experience.
records.localization_note: Make both qualifications explicit as Hodram considers inviting Cesare aboard.
records.previous_English: You know those lands. And you've been a captain...
records.english: You know those lands. And you've been a captain...

records.Japanese:
ならばこういうのはどうだ？
おまえは俺の船に乗り
俺の仕事を手伝う
records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.context: Hodram invites Cesare to join the crew and keep looking for his lost ship. Cesare offers a practical lesson on choosing ships. Hodram can hear the whole lesson or excuse him to make departure preparations.
records.source_meaning: Proposes that the man join his ship and help with his work.
records.localization_note: Restore Hodram's matter-of-fact offer to take Cesare aboard if he helps with his work.
records.previous_English: Here's a proposal. Join my ship and help me with my work.
records.english: Here's a proposal. Join my ship and help me with my work.

records.Japanese:
そうすれば、世界を周るうちに
おまえの船も見つかるだろう
records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.context: Hodram invites Cesare to join the crew and keep looking for his lost ship. Cesare offers a practical lesson on choosing ships. Hodram can hear the whole lesson or excuse him to make departure preparations.
records.source_meaning: Traveling around the world together should also offer a chance to find the missing ship.
records.localization_note: Hodram makes finding the ship a possibility while traveling with him.
records.previous_English: As we travel the world, we should be able to find your ship, too.
records.english: As we travel the world, we should be able to find your ship, too.

records.Japanese:
はは、FI提督
きっと、そうくると思いましたよ！
records.speaker: Charles Rochefort
records.context: Hodram invites Cesare to join the crew and keep looking for his lost ship. Cesare offers a practical lesson on choosing ships. Hodram can hear the whole lesson or excuse him to make departure preparations.

records.english: Ha! I knew you'd say that, Admiral FI!

records.Japanese:
ほ、本当ですか！
ぜひ、お願いするであります！
records.speaker: Cesare Tony
records.context: Hodram invites Cesare to join the crew and keep looking for his lost ship. Cesare offers a practical lesson on choosing ships. Hodram can hear the whole lesson or excuse him to make departure preparations.
records.source_meaning: The man gratefully and eagerly accepts.
records.localization_note: Cesare's startled acceptance keeps his eagerness and courteous address.
records.previous_English: Truly?! Please take me, sir!
records.english: Truly?! Please take me, sir!

records.Japanese:
来い、案内しよう。俺は
FI・FA
だ。期待しているぞ
records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.context: Hodram invites Cesare to join the crew and keep looking for his lost ship. Cesare offers a practical lesson on choosing ships. Hodram can hear the whole lesson or excuse him to make departure preparations.
records.source_meaning: Hodram offers to show him aboard, introduces himself as {MACRO:FI} {MACRO:FA} and says he has high expectations.

records.previous_English: Come along. I'll show you aboard. I'm FI FA. I'll be counting on you.
records.english: Come along. I'll show you aboard. I'm FI FA. I'll be counting on you.

records.Japanese: 私、チェザーレ・トーニであります
records.speaker: Cesare Tony
records.context: Hodram invites Cesare to join the crew and keep looking for his lost ship. Cesare offers a practical lesson on choosing ships. Hodram can hear the whole lesson or excuse him to make departure preparations.

records.localization_note: Cesare answers the introduction with his full name and a respectful address.
records.previous_English: Cesare Tony, sir!
records.english: Cesare Tony, sir!

records.Japanese:
よかったですね、チェザーレさん
私はシャルル・ロシュフォール
よろしく
records.speaker: Charles Rochefort
records.context: Hodram invites Cesare to join the crew and keep looking for his lost ship. Cesare offers a practical lesson on choosing ships. Hodram can hear the whole lesson or excuse him to make departure preparations.
records.source_meaning: Charles welcomes Cesare and introduces himself as Charles Rochefort.
records.localization_note: Charles welcomes Cesare and answers his introduction with his own name.
records.previous_English: Good for you, Cesare. Charles Rochefort. A pleasure.
records.english: Good for you, Cesare. Charles Rochefort. A pleasure.

records.Japanese:
あ、そうだ。提督殿
船の選び方について、私の意見を
聞いていただきたいのありますが…
records.speaker: Cesare Tony
records.context: Hodram invites Cesare to join the crew and keep looking for his lost ship. Cesare offers a practical lesson on choosing ships. Hodram can hear the whole lesson or excuse him to make departure preparations.

records.localization_note: Keep Cesare's polite request and the subject of the lesson he is about to offer.
records.previous_English: Oh, Admiral. May I offer some advice on choosing ships?
records.english: Oh, Admiral. May I offer some advice on choosing ships?

records.Japanese:
なるほど、お見それいたしました！
ご自分の主義がおありなのですね！
いやあ、素晴らしいことであります！
records.speaker: Cesare Tony
records.context: Hodram invites Cesare to join the crew and keep looking for his lost ship. Cesare offers a practical lesson on choosing ships. Hodram can hear the whole lesson or excuse him to make departure preparations.

records.previous_English: Understood! You have your own principles. Splendid, sir!
records.english: Understood! You have your own principles. Splendid, sir!

records.Japanese:
私は、これより出港準備に
とりかかります。ではでは！
records.speaker: Cesare Tony
records.context: Hodram invites Cesare to join the crew and keep looking for his lost ship. Cesare offers a practical lesson on choosing ships. Hodram can hear the whole lesson or excuse him to make departure preparations.

records.previous_English: I'll begin preparations to sail, then. Until later!
records.english: I'll begin preparations to sail, then. Until later!

records.Japanese: えー、では…
records.speaker: Cesare Tony
records.context: Hodram invites Cesare to join the crew and keep looking for his lost ship. Cesare offers a practical lesson on choosing ships. Hodram can hear the whole lesson or excuse him to make departure preparations.
records.source_meaning: In the advice branch, he begins his explanation.
records.localization_note: The short pause lets Cesare gather his thoughts before beginning his advice.
records.previous_English: Well then...
records.english: Well then...

records.Japanese:
ただ契約街を増やして航路を広げている
うちは、船を買う必要はありません
１％の契約では、買える交易品も
１つ～５つが限度ですからね
records.speaker: Cesare Tony
records.context: Hodram invites Cesare to join the crew and keep looking for his lost ship. Cesare offers a practical lesson on choosing ships. Hodram can hear the whole lesson or excuse him to make departure preparations.

records.english: Keep using the fleet you have while you sign deals with new towns and open trade routes. There's no need to buy more yet. With a one percent share, you can buy only one to five units of trade goods.

records.Japanese:
シェアが増えて
交易品がたくさん買えるようになったら
いよいよ船を買うときですね
records.speaker: Cesare Tony
records.context: Hodram invites Cesare to join the crew and keep looking for his lost ship. Cesare offers a practical lesson on choosing ships. Hodram can hear the whole lesson or excuse him to make departure preparations.
records.source_meaning: Once market share grows enough to buy many goods, it is time to acquire ships.
records.localization_note: Keep the increase in market share and the larger purchase volume as the reason to buy a ship.

records.english: Once your market share grows and you can buy more goods, it's time to buy a ship.

records.Japanese:
ここでまず考えるべきは
船の大きさと値段であります
records.speaker: Cesare Tony
records.context: Hodram invites Cesare to join the crew and keep looking for his lost ship. Cesare offers a practical lesson on choosing ships. Hodram can hear the whole lesson or excuse him to make departure preparations.
records.source_meaning: The first considerations are ship size and price.
records.localization_note: The topic sentence names both purchasing factors before explaining them.
records.previous_English: Consider ship size and price.
records.english: Consider ship size and price.

records.Japanese:
シェアと所持金に応じた船を選ばな
ければ、船一杯に積めるだけの交易品を
買えないのに、結局、水夫ばかり
必要になってしまいます

records.context: Hodram invites Cesare to join the crew and keep looking for his lost ship. Cesare offers a practical lesson on choosing ships. Hodram can hear the whole lesson or excuse him to make departure preparations.
records.source_meaning: A ship must match market share and funds; otherwise it demands more sailors without enough available merchandise to fill it.
records.localization_note: Keep the two sizing limits and the mismatch between cargo purchases and sailors. Let the consequence read as a full thought.
records.previous_English: Buy a ship your market share and budget can support. Otherwise you'll need more sailors for a ship you can't fill.
records.english: Buy a ship your market share and budget can support. Otherwise you'll need more sailors for a ship you can't fill.

records.Japanese:
船の大きさは、価格を見れば分かります
価格が５千未満なら小型船、１～２万
なら中型、５万をこえていたら
大型船といえます
records.speaker: Cesare Tony
records.context: Hodram invites Cesare to join the crew and keep looking for his lost ship. Cesare offers a practical lesson on choosing ships. Hodram can hear the whole lesson or excuse him to make departure preparations.
records.source_meaning: Price indicates size: below 5,000 is small, 10,000 to 20,000 medium, and above 50,000 large.

records.previous_English: Price gives you an idea of size. Under 5,000 is small, 10,000 to 20,000 is medium, and over 50,000 is large.
records.english: Price gives you an idea of size. Under 5,000 is small, 10,000 to 20,000 is medium, and over 50,000 is large.

records.Japanese:
小型船はとても安いので
手もとの資金に余裕がなくても
艦隊が運べる積み荷の数を簡単に
増やせます

records.english: Small ships are cheap. Even when funds are tight, they let you add cargo space to your fleet.

records.Japanese:
しばらく交易して
資金に余裕ができてきたなら
中型船に買い換えましょう
records.speaker: Cesare Tony
records.context: Hodram invites Cesare to join the crew and keep looking for his lost ship. Cesare offers a practical lesson on choosing ships. Hodram can hear the whole lesson or excuse him to make departure preparations.
records.source_meaning: After trading builds up funds, replace them with medium ships.
records.localization_note: The next upgrade follows the increase in funds from trading.
records.previous_English: After trading builds your funds, replace them with medium ships.
records.english: After trading builds your funds, replace them with medium ships.

records.Japanese:
中型船には２本マストと３本マストが
あります。もちろん、３本マストの
ほうが速いのですが、操帆手が
多く必要になるのであります

records.english: Medium ships come in two types. Some have two masts, others three. A third mast makes the ship faster, but you'll need more sail handlers.

records.Japanese:
改造すれば、積荷倉庫を最大の５部屋
まで取れます。当面の間、戦わない
つもりならば海兵詰所や砲台は
いりませんからね
records.speaker: Cesare Tony
records.context: Hodram invites Cesare to join the crew and keep looking for his lost ship. Cesare offers a practical lesson on choosing ships. Hodram can hear the whole lesson or excuse him to make departure preparations.
records.source_meaning: Refitting can provide the maximum five cargo holds; marine quarters and gun batteries are unnecessary if no fighting is planned for the time being.
records.localization_note: Keep the original upper limit and the condition for leaving out combat rooms.
records.previous_English: Refit for up to five cargo holds. If you won't fight for a while, skip marine quarters and batteries.
records.english: Refit for up to five cargo holds. If you won't fight for a while, skip marine quarters and batteries.

records.Japanese:
遠洋航海で遠くの街へ航路を
開きたいなら、物資倉庫の数を
増やせば、かなり遠くまで
航海できますよ
records.speaker: Cesare Tony
records.context: Hodram invites Cesare to join the crew and keep looking for his lost ship. Cesare offers a practical lesson on choosing ships. Hodram can hear the whole lesson or excuse him to make departure preparations.
records.source_meaning: For long ocean voyages opening distant routes, more supply holds extend sailing range considerably.
records.localization_note: Restore distant towns and route opening as the purpose of expanding supplies.
records.previous_English: To open a route to a distant town, add more supply holds. That lets you sail much farther.
records.english: To open a route to a distant town, add more supply holds. That lets you sail much farther.

records.Japanese:
誰か他の勢力と事を構えるようならば
やはり大型船が必要になりますです
records.speaker: Cesare Tony
records.context: Hodram invites Cesare to join the crew and keep looking for his lost ship. Cesare offers a practical lesson on choosing ships. Hodram can hear the whole lesson or excuse him to make departure preparations.
records.source_meaning: Conflict with another faction will make large ships necessary.
records.localization_note: The change from peaceful trade to conflict explains why large ships are needed.
records.previous_English: Conflict with another power will require large ships.
records.english: Conflict with another power will require large ships.

records.Japanese:
せめて旗艦だけでも、海兵詰所と
武装砲台を備えた船を用意しないと
なかなか海戦には勝つことは
できませんです

records.context: Hodram invites Cesare to join the crew and keep looking for his lost ship. Cesare offers a practical lesson on choosing ships. Hodram can hear the whole lesson or excuse him to make departure preparations.
records.source_meaning: At least the flagship should have marine quarters and armed batteries to make naval victories feasible.

records.english: Equip at least your flagship with marine quarters and armed batteries. It'll be hard to win at sea without them.

records.Japanese:
…あとは所持金との相談です
大型を１隻買うよりも、中型を２隻買う
方が安いし、交易品もたくさん
積めます

records.english: Mind your funds. Two medium ships cost less than one large ship and carry more goods.

records.Japanese:
いつかは大型船に買い換えることに
なりますが、将来、地方艦隊を作る
のであれば、お古の中型を売らずに
とっておいてもいいでしょう

records.english: You'll move up to large ships. Planning to form regional fleets? You could keep your medium ships.

records.Japanese:
私の意見は以上であります。私は
これより出港準備にとりかかります
ではでは！

records.source_meaning: Concludes the advice and excuses himself to prepare for departure.

records.previous_English: That's all my advice. I'll get ready to sail. Until later!
records.english: That's all my advice. I'll get ready to sail. Until later!

records.Japanese:
やあ、あんたたち
